g.text: C297 · Shot noise from dark current

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 7.1.2 (Dark current) · even with no light, the detector’s current flickers — and the flicker grows with bandwidth

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 1 · Dark current = a stream of random electrons

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: → current wobbles by ≈ 179 nA rms = the shot noise

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: end; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Monte Carlo toy, computed here (window = 1/(2·BW), BW = 10 GHz)

g.text: Slope ½ on log–log axes: 100× faster → only 10× more noise,

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: but more noise all the same. Less dark current → lower curve.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 4 · Faster detector → needs lower dark current

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 5 · But in a receiver, the amplifier often dominates the noise

text.style: font-size: 8.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Shot noise is usually the dominant noise factor in the

text.style: font-size: 8.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Ge-on-Si photodetector itself. Downstream, though, the

text.style: font-size: 8.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: electrical amplification often contributes most of the
